source_text:
Ἀντίψυχον ὑμῶν ἐγὼ καὶ ὧν ἐπέμψατε εἰς θεοῦ τιμὴν εἰς Σμύρναν, ὅθεν καὶ γράφω ὑμῖν, εὐχαριστῶν τῷ κυρίῳ, ἀγαπῶν Πολύκαρπον ὡς καὶ ὑμᾶς: μνημονεύετέ μου, ὡς καὶ ὑμῶν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός.
προσεύχεσθε ὑπὲρ τῆς ἐκκλησίας τῆς ἐν Συρίᾳ, ὅθεν δεδεμένος εἰς Ῥώμην ἀπάγομαι, ἔσχατος ὢν τῶν ἐκεῖ πιστῶν, ὥσπερ ἠξιώθην εἰς τιμὴν θεοῦ εὑρεθῆναι. ἔρρωσθε ἐν θεῷ πατρὶ καὶ ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ, τῇ κοινῇ ἐλπίδι ἡμῶν.
thought_title: Closing exchange of souls and farewell
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the Ephesians, speaking of himself as their ransom and asking their prayers for the church in Syria as he is taken to Rome.
pass_a_gloss: A ransom [for] you [am] I and [for] those whom you sent to [the] honor of God into Smyrna, from where also I write to you, giving thanks to the Lord, loving Polycarp as also you. Remember me, as also you [may] Jesus Christ [remember]. Pray for the church in Syria, from where bound to Rome I am led away, [being the] last of the faithful there, just as I was counted worthy for [the] honor of God to be found. Farewell in God [the] Father and in Jesus Christ, the common hope of us.

choices.why: The noun means a life given in exchange for another; 'ransom' keeps the substitutionary force without importing later theological weight.
The prepositional phrase marks purpose; keeping 'for the honor of God' preserves the final sense.

choices.english: though I am the least of the faithful there
choices.why: The participle with 'last' expresses a concessive self-description; 'least' is idiomatic for rank, not position.
rejected: being the last of the believers there
the last one among the faithful there

choices.why: The standard epistolary closing verb; 'farewell' is the conventional English equivalent.
The dative is in apposition to Jesus Christ; 'common' captures the shared, corporate sense of κοινῇ.

pass_b_english: I am a ransom for you and for those you sent to Smyrna for the honor of God. From Smyrna I am also writing to you, giving thanks to the Lord and loving Polycarp as I love you. Remember me, as Jesus Christ also remembers you.

Pray for the church in Syria, from where I am being led away to Rome in chains, though I am the least of the faithful there, just as I was counted worthy to be found for the honor of God. Farewell in God the Father and in Jesus Christ, our common hope.

last_rejected.quote: I am a ransom for you
last_rejected.why: ἀντίψυχον means 'substitute-life' or 'life given in exchange', not 'ransom' (which is λύτρον). Ignatius offers his life, not a payment.
last_rejected.fix: I am a substitute for your lives
last_rejected.ruling: ἀντίψυχον can mean 'ransom' or 'substitute'; both convey life given in exchange. Within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: as Jesus Christ also remembers you
last_rejected.why: The Greek has no verb; it means 'as Jesus Christ [does] of you' or 'as [he does] of you, Jesus Christ.' The subject is Jesus Christ remembering the Ephesians, not remembering Ignatius.
last_rejected.fix: as Jesus Christ does of you
last_rejected.ruling: No verb in Greek; 'remembers' supplied from context. Subject Jesus Christ is correct either way. Minor ellipsis fill.

last_rejected.quote: though I am the least of the faithful there
last_rejected.why: 'though' adds a concessive contrast absent in Greek. Ignatius states his low status as fact, not in tension with being counted worthy.
last_rejected.fix: I, the least of the faithful there
last_rejected.ruling: Participle ἔσχατος ὢν can carry concessive sense; 'though' is standard rendering. Not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: to be found for the honor of God
last_rejected.why: εὑρεθῆναι is passive 'to be found [by God]' or 'to be shown to be,' not purpose 'for.' The dative εἰς τιμὴν θεοῦ indicates God's honor is the standard or result, not the purpose.
last_rejected.fix: to be found worthy of God's honor
last_rejected.ruling: εἰς τιμὴν commonly denotes purpose/result; 'for the honor of God' is standard. εὑρεθῆναι passive rendered correctly.

last_rejected.why: εὐχαριστῶν is from εὐχαριστέω, not the noun εὐχαριστία. However, the glossary term εὐχαριστία = 'Eucharist' is not violated here. No glossary issue.
last_rejected.ruling: Reporter confirms no glossary issue exists. εὐχαριστῶν correctly rendered as 'giving thanks.'

polish.changed: Clarified that Ignatius is writing from Smyrna, made the sentence breaks follow the natural turns of thought, and kept every claim and reference intact while smoothing the rhythm for reading aloud.

variants.text: Polycarp, bishop of the church of Smyrna

notes.why: Polycarp's title varies; in 7.praef 'bishop of the church of Smyrna', elsewhere just 'Polycarp'.
notes.fix: Standardize or add note identifying Polycarp consistently.
